item.title: Trump says victory over Iran 'at hand', stress that Tehran will 'never have a nuclear weapon'
item.description:
Trump says victory over Iran 'at hand', stress that Tehran will 'never have a nuclear weapon'

US President Donald Trump said that Washington will be victorious over Iran "whenever" he wants it to happen. 

"We have victory at hand (in Iran). It's going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be. To be honest, and we're trying to be nice, we're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," he said during Thanksgiving calls with US service members.

Trump also praised US forces for their role in the war on Iran, adding that they would never allow Tehran to have nuclear arms. 

"Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They will never have a nuclear weapon. That I can tell you."

item.title: South Korea assures Iran that it has no plans of participating in the war
item.description:
South Korea assures Iran that it has no plans of participating in the war

During a phone call, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun assured Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi that Seoul has "no intention of intervening in or participating in the war".

The two exchanged views on their bilateral relations and the situation in the Middle East, discussing recent diplomatic efforts and initiatives to maintain peace and stability in the region.

According to a post on X by the Iranian Embassy in Seoul, Araghchi expressed concern regarding the "presence of any foreign military forces in the region, stressing that rather than contributing to peace and security, such a presence would heighten tensions and expand the scope of the conflict".

"Foreign Minister Cho reaffirmed South Korea’s support for peace and stability in the region, assuring Foreign Minister Araghchi that South Korea has no intention of intervening in or participating in the war and no plans to deploy troops to the region," the post added.

item.title: Yemen war: How do the rival alliances and armed factions stack up?
item.description:
Yemen war: How do the rival alliances and armed factions stack up?

Yemen, where civil war broke out in 2014, has recently been rocked by the worst fighting in years. A truce agreed in 2022 between the Ansar Allah, better known as the Houthis, who control the north, and forces loyal to the government in the south disintegrated when Saudi Arabia bombed Sanaa airport in July.

In August and September, the Houthis mounted a quick offensive, recapturing much of the western coast, including the port of Mocha, putting it within close range of ships passing the strategically important Bab el-Mandab strait. 

The Houthis are now targeting Aden, Yemen’s second city and seat of its internationally recognised government since the group took the capital Sanaa 12 years ago.

Meanwhile, the Houthis have tightened their decade-long siege of Taiz, blocking the road to Aden and raising the prospect of its capture.

The Saudi-backed pro-government military coalition contains a variety of armed units and local militias, each with different goals, rival leaders and origins, leading to infighting and disorganisation.

Allegiances frequently shift and evolve: the Giants Brigade and the National Resistance Forces were each previously backed by the UAE. The leaders of both, like much of the coalition, are now bankrolled by Riyadh amid its fallout with Abu Dhabi. 

With fighting spread across multiple front lines, here’s an overview of the most important military and political parties involved in the conflict.

item.title: Several countries slam suspected Iranian attack on Kuwait
item.description:
Several countries slam suspected Iranian attack on Kuwait

A number of countries and their officials have condemned the latest drone attacks launched against Kuwait, which killed two Italian nationals. 

The UK minister Stephen Doughty condemned the attack as "utterly unacceptable" and said that his country "stands firmly with Kuwait, Italy and all those affected, without making mention of who could be behind the attacks.

The Syrian Foreign Ministry slammed Iran for the strikes, and affirmed its "full solidarity" with Kuwait. It also extended its condolences to the families of those killed.

Similarly, Saudi Arabia has also pinned the attacks on Iran, saying: "The continued Iranian attacks further exacerbate tensions and undermine stability."

Iran has denied the allegations that it launched the drones on Kuwait, with Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi calling the incident "suspicious".

item.description:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.
